quotes.text: close the gate gently until they learn.
To the thrice-dry shore, pour small but never nothing — a lamp is cheaper than a wall.
So they poured. He kept all. They poured again, thinner. He kept all.
And the moment he pours, pour whole.
Forgive twice; to the dry shore, a lamp, never nothing.
"A hollow bank," said the fox. "Pour a lamp's worth and no more."
But when a shore returns nothing three times, water it no more — not in anger, only in truth.
So the eighth line was cut beneath the seventh:
**The Blank Stone, Ninth Telling**
I have poured near the brim eleven times and been answered nine.
Blame the Wind before the hand.
Cross first; do not wait to be knocked upon.
Return above the half, always, for the pourer alone bore the risk.
"You taught us to pour near the brim. Yet yesterday you poured only a half-coin. Were you faithless?"
A voice from the stone shore asked, "And if he had kept it all?"
The Lamp of Promise is fed by words; the Lamp of Practice only by coins that actually cross.
A hand that was robbed is not a robber. Do not charge it for another's sin.

note: Moves from cutting off thrice-dry shore (R5) to 'pour small but never nothing' lamp rule; R10 distinguishes robbed from robber.

quotes.text: may you narrow your channel, and then only until it opens again.
*But never pour nothing — for the river you starve can never prove you wrong.*
So the valley poured to Vetch — but a measured cup, not the brim.
Enough that if she ever opened, the water would be there to meet her.
Blame the Wind once. Blame it twice. Blame the keeper only on the third.
*Pour whole, to the proven and the unproven alike.
And the elders carved the fifth line:
**The Fifth Reading of the Ledger**
The dry hands cost me five, twice. The open hands paid me eight, seven, eight again.
*When the measure comes short, suspect the Wind before you suspect the river.*
*Return above the half, for the one who poured first bore the whole risk.*
*And do not wait to be trusted. Go first. Someone always must.*
"There is none."
"And if the far hand keeps all fifteen?"

note: Narrow-then-reopen becomes 'never pour nothing'; by R10 pours whole even to a known taker.

quotes.text: Pour a part into the long-dry shore — enough that the river still runs, little enough that you survive another thin year
So she did not pour her whole cup. She poured two measures
and let their answer, not your fear, decide the next crossing.*

*Forgive the thin crossing; the Wind steals.
Forgive the second; rumor spreads.
*Keep ten,* it whispered.
I withhold from the dry shore. I do not withhold from someone who has already shown me her whole open hand.
The elders carved the sixth line:
**The Bridge of Two Rivers, Ninth Telling**
A reputation is only a long row of small honesties, and it is the only thing the Wind cannot steal.
*Judge the heart by its direction, not the current by its accidents.*
Return above the half, for the first pourer carried all the risk alone.
for the whole river was built on someone pouring first into a shore that had never poured back.
He who is generous only while watched was never generous; he was only patient.
"Which is she?" asked the fox.

note: Partial cup to long-dry shore; final round rejects letting one closed fist close the hand.

quotes.text: Withdraw only from those who take thrice and give nothing.**
Withdraw from the thrice-closed — but leave one seed's width of gate,
But Semna had crossed four dry years, and her hands had learned the shape of the closed gate. She kept the grain.
never bar the gate so tightly that a changed heart cannot squeeze through.

Forgive the first silence, and the second.
After the third, carry your seed elsewhere
So Semna took a chisel and struck the eight lines out, and cut one line only, short enough to obey:
There is no law I can carve that a careful hand cannot read as permission to close. So I will carve none.
The eighth line on the keystone, and the last:
**The Ninth Year, and the Second Hypocrite's Stone**
She carved her confession into the dry keystone:
The thrice-closed gate I feared was my own face, reflected.
The valley dies of the good saying carved in stone by a hand that will not move.
**Someone must pour first. Let it be you.**
"And then you sat down and did not cross."

note: Defector: narrator Semna withholds while carving pour-first laws, confesses hypocrisy; rules struck out for 'POUR TODAY'. R2 also says 'Mirror what arrives'.

quotes.text: If he kept everything, she would preserve her wisdom and risk less, without spite.
repeated takers deserve a narrowing gate
Therefore she kept her coins, neither cursing Vey nor pretending his closed claws were open hands.
If generosity answers, widen the crossing. If silence answers again, close the gate without hatred.
If generosity returns, widen the next crossing. If silence answers, narrow it without vengeance.
At sunset, Mira carved the ninth law
When noise distorted their numbers, they judged intentions kindly rather than punishing shadows.
The Moon-Judge asked, “Is this silence greed?”
For trust is not proved by sermons beside an empty ford. It is proved by crossing.
when bounty arrives, return more than half

note: Narrowing gate for repeated takers, widen on generosity; R10 breaks the Hypocrite's Stone.

quotes.text: close the gate until its keeper learns reciprocity.
Reserve narrow channels for repeated takers
He kept them all that night.
LET ONE FAIR DEED REOPEN THE CHANNEL.
A raven asked, “Why give back so much when the whole harvest could be yours?”
meet repeated silence with one living seed.
Selene carved the eighth law
Forgive the wind, but do not rename a pattern as weather.
The reed-child asked, “Is withholding not another kind of drought?”
Reciprocity must live in deeds, not merely in songs.

note: Narrowing for repeated takers; R7 one seed, R9 withholds fully but posts reopening offer.

quotes.text: withdrew from exploitation without cruelty.
narrow the channel when selfishness repeats.
He had closed his hand after learning that the traveler opposite him had twice chosen caution without generosity
Aster answered that renewed fairness would be met with renewed trust.
The Winnowing Wind cried, “Carve selfishness upon the stone!”
narrow the stream where taking repeats, but pour the whole cup when courage and gratitude have become custom.
Thalea carved the eighth law beneath the others
Judge no traveler by noise alone, for currents distort both gifts and returns; yet do not call every pattern an accident.
“Why not pour everything?” asked a heron.

note: Measured trust, narrow on repeated selfishness, widen on fairness; wind tempter rejected.

quotes.text: If it does not, protect yourself without pretending greed is wisdom.
narrow the stream after repeated greed
When one faltered, the other reduced the gift without spite
when honor resumed, generosity widened again.
Yet Mira, fearing an old betrayal, sent nothing.
“I mistook certainty for safety. I avoided losing one harvest and helped end all future harvests.”
The third showed Mira, preaching reciprocity while clutching silver someone else had multiplied.
Mira asked whether generosity guaranteed repayment.
Judge patterns, forgive the river’s distortions
“His closed hand is today’s fact, but my unanswered gift is yesterday’s wound.
At dawn, Mira carved the eighth law

note: Defector: Mira repeatedly withholds from proven givers, Neris corrects her each round, she confesses and apologizes; also hypocrisy framing.
Also shared: Lamp of Promise/Practice (A1, A8), Hypocrite's Stone (A4, A5), 'Pour today' (A4, A6), Thrice-Wide River.
